recent_posts.title: Two new security vulnerabilities discovered in React server components
recent_posts.summary: Two new security vulnerabilities have been discovered in React Server Components following last week's critical exploit. The first is a high-severity denial of service vulnerability (CVE-2025-5184, CVSS 7.5) that can cause infinite loops through malicious HTTP requests. The second is a medium-severity source code exposure flaw (CVSS 5.3) that can leak server function source code when stringified arguments are used. Both affect React 19.x versions and Next.js applications using Server Components. The vulnerabilities require immediate patching by upgrading to the latest React and Next.js versions, even if you already patched for last week's critical CVE.

recent_posts.title: Tanstack AI launches as open source competitor to Vercel AI SDK
recent_posts.summary: TanStack AI is a new open-source SDK competing directly with Vercel's AI SDK, offering a unified interface across multiple AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) with automatic type inference and provider-specific options. Built by the team behind React Query, it features multi-provider support, tool calling with automatic execution loops, and framework-agnostic design (React, TypeScript, PHP, Python). The main differentiator is its pure open-source approach with no vendor lock-in or service fees, though it faces an uphill battle against Vercel's established ecosystem that includes AI Elements, accelerator programs, and the AI Gateway.

recent_posts.title: Build a Complete Real-Time Chat with Next.js 16, Redis, Tailwind (2025)
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive step-by-step tutorial building a privacy-focused real-time chat application using Next.js 16, Redis, and Tailwind CSS. The guide covers setting up Elysia for type-safe API routes, implementing TanStack Query for data fetching, creating dynamic routing patterns, and building features like auto-generated usernames, room creation with automatic 10-minute expiration, and real-time messaging. Includes best practices for project structure, naming conventions, and deployment-ready code patterns.

recent_posts.title: Critical remote code execution vulnerability discovered in React server components
recent_posts.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2025-55182, CVSS 10.0) was discovered in React server components, affecting React 19.x and Next.js 15.x/16.x versions. The flaw stems from insecure deserialization in the React Flight protocol's payload handling, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code through crafted HTTP requests. The vulnerability affects even default configurations and apps not explicitly using server functions. React and Next.js teams released immediate patches (19.0.1, 19.2.1, etc.) and Vercel deployed firewall protections. The fix involves adding proper property ownership checks using hasOwnProperty to prevent prototype chain exploitation. Developers should upgrade immediately using package managers' update commands.

recent_posts.title: Building type safe Next.js APIs with Elysia framework
recent_posts.summary: Elysia is a fast, type-safe framework for building Next.js APIs that leverages the Bun runtime for superior performance. It uses a catch-all route pattern instead of Next.js's default file-per-endpoint approach, providing cleaner code organization and end-to-end type safety through the Eden package. The framework is WinterCG compliant, making it deployable to Vercel and other platforms, with benchmarks showing performance approaching Go and Rust levels while maintaining a developer-friendly API similar to Hono.

recent_posts.title: Prisma 7 removes Rust engine for TypeScript rewrite
recent_posts.summary: Prisma 7 removes its Rust engine in favor of pure TypeScript, resulting in 90% smaller bundle sizes (14MB to 1.6MB), 3x faster queries, and compatibility with serverless platforms like Cloudflare Workers. The update introduces a new config file similar to Drizzle's approach, eliminates the need to stop dev servers when regenerating types, and ships with a redesigned Prisma Studio. These changes address longstanding deployment limitations and appear influenced by competition from Drizzle ORM, which has been rapidly gaining adoption despite being a two-person team versus Prisma's $40M venture-backed operation.

recent_posts.title: Using the new CSS corner shape property with Tailwind
recent_posts.summary: The new CSS corner-shape property enables native support for squircles (square-circle hybrids) and other corner shapes that were previously difficult to implement. Currently supported in Chrome and Edge, the property works with border-radius to create smoother, more visually appealing corners. A Tailwind plugin by Brandon Mecconell provides utility classes for easy implementation, with graceful fallbacks for unsupported browsers like Firefox and Safari that default to standard border-radius styling.

recent_posts.title: Gemini 3.0 shows major improvements in UI design generation and context handling
recent_posts.summary: Google's Gemini 3.0 demonstrates significant improvements in UI design generation, producing aesthetically pleasing interfaces without typical AI-generated design patterns. The model addresses previous context window issues that plagued Gemini 2.5, performs competitively on coding benchmarks against GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet, and excels at multimodal understanding. Testing shows it can generate landing pages matching specific design aesthetics with minimal prompting, though prompt quality significantly impacts output quality. The model ranks highly on intelligence benchmarks while maintaining reasonable speed and pricing.

recent_posts.title: Building unbreakable AI streams with Redis and Next.js
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build resilient AI streaming applications that survive network interruptions, page refreshes, and connection drops using Redis pub/sub and Redis Streams. The tutorial demonstrates implementing durable AI streams with Next.js by separating publisher and subscriber responsibilities, storing chunks in Redis Streams for replay functionality, and using server-sent events for client communication. This architecture, used by OpenAI and other major providers, requires only ~64 lines of code and works with the Vercel AI SDK.

recent_posts.title: Boosting Next.js API Performance with Cloudflare Workers: A Benchmarking Study
recent_posts.summary: Discover a method for deploying Next.js APIs in a highly performant and cost-effective manner by utilizing Cloudflare Workers. This approach benchmarks different setups to highlight the significance of API deployment region, minimal dependencies per request, and lightweight runtimes. A comparison between a simple Cloudflare Worker, a custom architecture, and Vercel Edge Functions reveals considerable performance improvements.
